info.description: Cases, marks and screenshots of a team, and the operations that change them. Version 1 only grows: fields and paths are added, never removed or changed. Ignore what you do not know.

get.summary: One case as a file: the zip the Sitegloss extension exports
get.description: The case in the extension's file format (`sitegloss/1`): `case.json`, `case.md`, the screenshots in `shots/` and the marks' crops in `crops/`, as the extension's own export lays them out. The extension's Import a case… reads it; an AI agent reads it as files. Stored entries, no zip64: a case larger than 4 GiB is refused (413). Who may read the case may download it.

AppRef.description: An AI app: its client id, the name it declares, and a host: of its id when that is an address, else of where its sign-in returns to.

Backdrop.description: The colour that shows behind the element: its own background colour or, while that is transparent or translucent, composited over its ancestors' until an opaque one. color: as computed. depth: how many steps up the opaque background is (0: the element itself), an integer of at most 1,000; with depth, an opaque background was found that many steps up. Without depth no contrast ratio holds: either no opaque background was found up to the page and color is the browser's default canvas for the page's colour scheme (not measured), or color is in a form that was not worked out (for instance oklch(...)) and is given as written, or a malformed depth was dropped. image: true when a background image or gradient on the way may show instead of the colour. The server drops the whole backdrop when color is empty, longer than 300 characters or names a URL (as a style value), and depth when it is not such an integer; not refused. Hard bound: color of at most 2,000 characters.

Case.description: A case: marks on one or more pages of a site.

CaseComment.description: One comment in a case's thread: what someone (or an AI app for them) says about the case or one of its marks, beside the summary, which stays the reporter's.

CaseCounts.description: A case's marks by status group.

Changes.description: Everything that changed in a team after a revision.

ClientInfo.description: The browser the case was started in.

ElementDetails.description: What is recorded about a mark's element.

ElementStyles.description: Computed CSS of the element when the mark was made: property name to its value as the browser computed it. Data, shown as text only. Which properties is the client's choice. The server keeps at most 40 entries (the first ones), each with a name of a-z, digits and - (a vendor prefix allowed, never a custom property `--x`) of at most 60 characters and a value of at most 300 characters that names no URL (url(, image(, image-set(, cross-fade(, element(, src(, paint(, :// or a quoted path, also behind CSS escapes or comments); what does not fit is dropped, not refused. Hard bounds, which make the request invalid: at most 200 entries, names of 200 and values of 2,000 characters.

Finding.description: What an AI app found out about a mark.

Id.description: An id: letters, digits, _ and -, at most 64.

ImageRef.description: A WebP image, named by the SHA-256 of its bytes.

MarkEnds.description: The page elements at the two ends of a stroke (an arrow, an open pen stroke), as the extension recorded them when the mark was made. Set with the mark, never changed afterwards.

MarkStatus.description: Derived from the resolution, never stored.

query.description: The query of the address the screenshot was taken at, without the leading `?`. The server keeps what `keptQuery` (DEC-023) keeps of it: pieces whose name says secret (token, key, code, session, email and the like) or whose value looks like one (an e-mail address, a JWT, a long opaque value) are dropped, and a query longer than 1024 characters after that is dropped whole. Never refused for what it holds; only one longer than 8000 UTF-16 units, the most a whole address holds, makes the request invalid, which a client that filters first never sends. A client should filter it the same way before sending.

Op.description: One change to a case, a screenshot, a mark or a comment. A server that does not know an operation's type refuses the request; a client sends only the types it knows.

OpErrorCode.description: Why an operation was refused. A client treats a code it does not know as invalid.

Page.description: A page of the case: origin, path and hash route, no query. A case lists a page once, and a page is its path in whatever environment: `https://shop.example/cart` and `http://localhost:3000/cart/` are one page, two sites' home pages are two (the rule and its test cases: `pageKey` and `vectors/page-key.json` in the API package). The server keeps the list: a screenshot of a page the case does not have adds it, and a page leaves with its last screenshot, except the last page of all.

Reopen.description: One time a settled mark was opened again, with the resolution it ended.

Resolution.description: How a mark was settled. verified only with kind fixed.

Shape.description: A mark's drawing, in CSS pixels of its screenshot.

query.description: The query of the address the screenshot was taken at, without the leading `?`: what `keptQuery` (DEC-023) keeps of it, in the order and encoding it came in, at most 1024 characters. Absent when there is none. `url` stays the plain address (origin, path and hash route) that pages are matched by; this is for opening the page again, before the hash. Only a team's members get it: never a share link.

Shot.description: A screenshot of one page of the case. Never changes once created.

SiblingBox.description: The box of one of the element's nearest element siblings. offset: its place relative to the element, an integer from -100 to 100, never 0 (-1 the sibling right before it, 1 the one right after). tag: the element's name (a letter, then letters, digits, -, _, . or :; at most 100). rect: in the same document CSS pixels as the element's rect. The server drops a sibling whose offset or tag is not so, and keeps the first 6; not refused.

Stamp.description: Who did something, and when: the person (set by the server from the caller's login, never taken from a client) and the AI app they acted through. Written in words: `Dana via Claude Code`.

UserRef.description: A person. Set by the server from the caller's login, never taken from a client.

Viewport.description: The window in CSS pixels; dpr: screenshot pixels per CSS pixel.

oauth.description: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. Ask for the resource `<origin>/api` to get a token for this API. Discovery: `<origin>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/api/auth`.
